recent_posts.title: How to use Cursor for real software development tasks
recent_posts.summary: A practical walkthrough of using Cursor, the AI-powered VSCode fork, for everyday software development tasks. Covers the three core features — Autocomplete, Ask, and Agent — along with tips on managing context, choosing the right LLM model, and applying these tools to real use cases like generating tests, writing documentation, code review, onboarding to new codebases, refactoring, and building new features. Also includes tricks like attaching screenshots for UI generation and using Cursor Rules to handle newer library APIs the model wasn't trained on.

recent_posts.title: AI Is Speeding Up Development. But Where Are the New Bottlenecks?
recent_posts.summary: Autonomous coding agents are becoming core to modern development workflows. Key differentiating features include customizable system prompts and rules for tailoring agent behavior, usage-based pricing to maximize model context, autonomous multi-phase workflows, background task execution, MCP-based tool integrations (Jira, GitHub, Confluence), and support for multiple AI model providers. Teams that invest in configuring these agents to their specific workflows stand to gain significant productivity improvements.

recent_posts.title: Making AI Deliver: From Pilots to Measurable Business Impact
recent_posts.summary: A panel discussion from the Leadership Exchange explores how organizations can move beyond AI experimentation to achieve measurable business results. Key themes include structured budgeting for AI initiatives, aligning AI projects with corporate strategy, and the governance and workflow integration needed to scale pilots into production. Panelists noted that agentic workflows and reduced human-in-the-loop processes represent the next frontier, reshaping team collaboration across departments.

recent_posts.title: Understanding Sourcemaps: From Development to Production
recent_posts.summary: Sourcemaps bridge the gap between minified production code and readable source code, enabling effective debugging. They work by creating JSON mappings between transformed and original code, with options for inline, external, or hidden implementations. While essential in development, production sourcemaps require careful consideration—they improve error tracking and debugging but can expose code structure and internal logic. Best practices include restricting access via server configuration, using services like Sentry for private sourcemap uploads, and ensuring no sensitive data exists in client code. The choice depends on your security requirements and debugging needs.

recent_posts.title: How to implement Vercel BotID for invisible bot protection
recent_posts.summary: Vercel BotID is an invisible CAPTCHA solution that protects web applications from sophisticated bots without disrupting real users. The tool uses lightweight browser signals to detect automated traffic in real-time, protecting critical endpoints like checkout flows, signup forms, and APIs. Implementation involves installing the SDK, configuring route protection on the client side, and verifying requests on the server using the checkBotId() function. BotID offers two modes: Basic Mode for all plans and Deep Analysis Mode with Kasada-powered detection for Pro and Enterprise users. The system maintains a directory of verified legitimate bots that can be selectively allowed, and developers can customize responses to failed checks ranging from hard blocks to soft failures.

recent_posts.title: Implementing Dynamic Types in Docusign Extension Apps
recent_posts.summary: Explores the implementation of dynamic types in Docusign Extension Apps, contrasting them with static types. Shows how dynamic types enable project-specific customization by retrieving type definitions from external systems at runtime, using a TaskVibe integration example. Covers the technical implementation of GetTypeNames and GetTypeDefinitions endpoints, handling custom fields, and managing Docusign's type definition caching behavior.

recent_posts.title: The simplicity of deploying an MCP server Vercel
recent_posts.summary: Vercel offers excellent hosting for Next.js applications but requires careful cost management due to its serverless, usage-based pricing model. The platform charges through two components: the Developer Experience Platform (monthly per-seat pricing) and Managed Infrastructure (usage-based). Key cost factors include function invocations, execution time, bandwidth usage, and image transformations. To control costs, developers should optimize serverless function calls, implement proper caching, minimize bandwidth through image optimization and efficient API responses, and use Vercel's monitoring tools with spending alerts. The platform offers Hobby (free, non-commercial), Pro ($20/member), and Enterprise (custom) plans, each with different resource limits and features.

recent_posts.title: Quo v[AI]dis, Tech Stack?
recent_posts.summary: AI coding tools are fundamentally reshaping how developers choose tech stacks, creating self-reinforcing loops that favor popular frameworks like React and Node.js. These tools perform better with widely-used technologies due to more training data, leading to increased adoption and further reinforcement. While AI enables faster development and makes developers more polyglot, it also introduces risks of vendor lock-in through AI-generated app bundles and may prioritize convenience over long-term maintainability. The shift from "buy vs build" to "prompt vs buy" is changing product development strategies, but teams must remain intentional about stack choices rather than defaulting to AI-suggested paths.

recent_posts.title: Next.js + MongoDB Connection Storming
recent_posts.summary: Vercel offers excellent hosting for Next.js applications but requires careful cost management due to its serverless, usage-based pricing model. Key cost factors include function invocations (from server actions, API routes, and React server component renders), execution time, bandwidth usage, and image transformations. To control costs, developers should batch server actions, minimize backend calls, optimize caching strategies, reduce bundle sizes, and configure image optimization settings. Vercel provides monitoring tools and spending alerts to help track usage against plan limits, with options to pause projects during unexpected traffic spikes.

recent_posts.title: Advanced Authentication and Onboarding Workflows with Docusign Extension Apps
recent_posts.summary: Docusign Extension Apps typically use OAuth 2 for authentication, but many external systems don't support it. This guide demonstrates how to extend the OAuth 2 flow by creating custom authorization and token endpoints that act as a bridge between Docusign and non-OAuth systems. The approach involves capturing user credentials through a custom form, encoding them in JWT tokens, and storing them securely on Docusign's side while maintaining the Extension App as a stateless proxy. The implementation uses Next.js to handle both frontend forms and backend API endpoints.
